parsed.title: Workflow contract contradiction: REPLAN-ROUTE branch destination
parsed.detail: The closing-block decision table in fold-findings/SKILL.md (line 184) states that for branch `REPLAN-ROUTE`, the consumer action is: `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>` → the planner it names re-cuts the plan, then `/review-plan` before `/execute-phase` on this unit`. However, the `fold-findings` skill's own `→ Next:` block (line 165) and the `REPAIR-RECEIPT` branch field definition (line 135) define the branch value as `REPLAN-ROUTE`. The `workflow-status` skill's `SENSOR_SIGNALS.md` (line 74) defines the trigger for this state as `{command: "/plan-feature <unit>" | "/plan-fix <issue>"...}`. The `fold-findings` doc instructs the consumer to run the router *then* review-plan, but the `workflow-status` sensor signal suggests the *planner* command directly. More critically, `fold-findings` line 184 implies the consumer runs the router, but `plan-feature` and `plan-fix` skills (lines 58-60 and 107-111 respectively) state that `unit-route.mjs` is run *internally* by the planner skill to determine if it should append phases. The `fold-findings` doc breaks the abstraction by exposing the internal router script to the consumer/hand-off, whereas other docs (e.g., `triage-issue` line 112) correctly route to `unit-route → plan-feature / plan-fix`. The `fold-findings` doc's `→ Next:` block is inconsistent with the `workflow-status` sensor's `next.suggested` output which lists the planner command, not the router script.

parsed.title: Usage-docs: Router invocation in hand-off vs internal step
parsed.detail: In `plan-feature/SKILL.md` line 58, step 4 of 'Progressive loading' says: 'Only when `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <NN>` prints `route: replan`: load the [replan contract]...'. This implies the *user* or *consumer* runs the router. However, in `plan-feature/references/ROUTING.md` line 10, it says: 'Before the status gate, run `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <NN>`... A `route: replan` line means... skip the STOP and load [the replan contract]...'. This is consistent. BUT, `fold-findings/SKILL.md` line 184 tells the *consumer* (after fold-findings) to run the router. `plan-feature` is a skill *invoked by the consumer*. If the consumer runs `plan-feature`, does `plan-feature` run the router internally, or does the consumer run the router *before* invoking `plan-feature`? The `plan-feature` skill's 'Progressive loading' step 4 suggests the *skill* (or the agent running the skill) checks the router. If the agent running `plan-feature` is expected to run the router, then `fold-findings` telling the consumer to run it is redundant or conflicting. More importantly, `plan-fix` (line 107) has the same structure. The defect is that `fold-findings` exposes the internal implementation detail (`scripts/unit-route.mjs`) in its `→ Next:` block (line 184), whereas `triage-issue` (line 112) and `workflow-status` (line 74) abstract this to `unit-route → plan-feature / plan-fix` or just the planner command. This breaks the 'brand' of the workflow where the router is an internal deterministic engine, not a user-facing command.

parsed.title: Spec-drift: Replan hand-off description mismatch
parsed.detail: In `PERSIST_AND_DECIDE.md` line 135, the `→ Next:` block for `REVIEW-FAIL` says: 'any finding routed replan-in-unit or owned by plan? → `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>` prints `route: replan` and names the planner...'. This instructs the user/consumer to run the router script. However, `plan-feature` and `plan-fix` are the skills that *consume* the replan route. The `fold-findings` skill also instructs the consumer to run the router. This creates a broken hand-off: the consumer is expected to run an internal script (`unit-route.mjs`) rather than invoking a skill. The `workflow-status` sensor (line 74) suggests `/plan-feature` or `/plan-fix`. The `PERSIST_AND_DECIDE` doc contradicts the `workflow-status` sensor's output contract by exposing the internal script.

parsed.title: Workflow: Inconsistent replan routing instruction
parsed.detail: In `triage-issue/SKILL.md` line 112, the diagram shows `replan-in-unit` routing to `unit-route → plan-feature / plan-fix`. The text below says: 'In review-finding mode, `replan-in-unit` runs `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>`...'. This is consistent with the diagram. However, compare this to `fold-findings` (line 184) which tells the consumer to run the router. `triage-issue` is a user-invocable skill. If `triage-issue` is invoked by a user, does the *user* run the router, or does `triage-issue` run it? The text says 'runs `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>`', implying the skill/agent runs it. But `fold-findings` tells the *consumer* (after the skill finishes) to run it. This is a contradiction in *who* runs the router. `fold-findings` says the consumer runs it; `triage-issue` says the skill runs it (or implies the agent running the skill runs it). This ambiguity breaks the workflow contract.
